paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: faith shows up in how you live, not only in what you say. Paul's team could have asked the church to support them, and Paul says they had the right (2 Thessalonians 3:9). They worked night and day instead, so they would be an example to imitate (2 Thessalonians 3:8-9). Some in the church were "accomplishing nothing, but being busybodies" (2 Thessalonians 3:11), and Paul's answer is to begin working quietly to earn their own living (2 Thessalonians 3:12).

Now notice HOW Paul asks for this. The command comes in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ (2 Thessalonians 3:6), so steady, honest work isn't a side issue. It's part of following Him. And when someone won't obey, the church keeps its distance so he may be ashamed, but he's still a brother to admonish, not an enemy (2 Thessalonians 3:14-15). I think that's love with its sleeves rolled up. It's firm and it's kind, and I'm still learning how to do both at once.

So what do you do with that today? Do the work in front of you, and "do not grow weary in well-doing" (2 Thessalonians 3:13). Some days that's the boring, quiet stuff nobody claps for, and that's fine. Paul closes with "the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way" (2 Thessalonians 3:16), and with grace from our Lord Jesus Christ for all of them (2 Thessalonians 3:18). You don't work to earn His love, friend. You work because you already have it.
